user.title: Set up BRUH Minecraft
user.description:
This integration talks to the BRUH Minecraft add-on running on this Home Assistant host. The add-on exposes sensors, buttons, and services for controlling your Minecraft server.

Server files live at `{server_dir}` and backups at `{backup_dir}`.

confirm.title: BRUH Minecraft discovered
confirm.description: Confirm setup to enable sensors, buttons, and services.

rcon_command.name: Run RCON command
rcon_command.description: Execute an arbitrary server command (no leading slash).

say.name: Broadcast chat
say.description: Send a chat message to all players.

give.name: Give item
give.description: Give an item to a specific player.

restart_server.name: Restart server
restart_server.description: Save worlds and restart the Minecraft server.

stop_server.name: Stop server
stop_server.description: Stop the Minecraft server (add-on stays running).

kick_player.name: Kick player
kick_player.description: Kick a player from the server.

ban_player.name: Ban player
ban_player.description: Ban a player from the server.

whitelist_add.name: Whitelist add
whitelist_add.description: Add a player to the whitelist.

whitelist_remove.name: Whitelist remove
whitelist_remove.description: Remove a player from the whitelist.

pardon_player.name: Unban player
pardon_player.description: Lift a ban on a player.

teleport.name: Teleport player
teleport.description: Move a player to another player, or to x/y/z coordinates.

player.name: Player
player.description: Who to move — a player name, or @a for everyone.

to_player.name: To player
to_player.description: The player to move them to. Leave empty to use x/y/z.

x.name: X
x.description: A number, or ~ / ~5 relative to where they are.

y.name: Y
y.description: A number, or ~ / ~5 relative to where they are.

z.name: Z
z.description: A number, or ~ / ~5 relative to where they are.

get_status.name: Get status
get_status.description: Who is online right now, beside the last collected server stats. Returns response data.

get_world.name: Get world
get_world.description: What is going on in the world now - who is on and where, the time, day and weather, recent events, the last save and backup, and the companion's builds. Returns response data.

list_builds.name: List builds
list_builds.description: The companion's build log, newest first. Returns response data.

save_build.name: Save build
save_build.description: Add a job to the companion's build log (give a title), or change one (give its id). A job set to done with bounds gets a top-down picture.

id.name: Job id
id.description: The job to change. Leave out to add a new one.

part.name: Part of the engine
part.description: Which part of the sentience engine this build is for (any label).

bounds.name: Bounds
bounds.description: The build's box: x1, z1, x2, z2, optional y1, y2 and dimension.

notes.name: Notes
notes.description: Anything worth keeping about the build.

image.name: Picture
image.description: A picture of the build (a /local/ path or URL), if not drawn from the world.

delete_build.name: Delete build
delete_build.description: Remove a job from the companion's build log.

list_addons.name: List add-ons
list_addons.description: What the add-on browser can offer this server, and what is installed in the active world. Returns response data.

search_addons.name: Search add-ons
search_addons.description: Search Modrinth for server-side add-ons this server can run (every player gets them, Bedrock/iPad included). Returns response data.

install_addon.name: Install add-on
install_addon.description: Add a Modrinth project (and anything it requires) to the active world.

id.name: Project id
id.description: The Modrinth project id from search_addons.

remove_addon.name: Remove add-on
remove_addon.description: Take an add-on installed by the browser out of the active world.

get_companion.name: Companion
get_companion.description: The companion's hands in the game — who it is (the name and colour brAIn last set), the named places, the choice-pad questions, the action log (each undoable action has an id), what it said, and whether the server checks the accounts behind the names in chat. Returns response data.

set_companion.name: Set the companion
set_companion.description: Tell the add-on who the companion is, for its panel and as the default speaker. A companion (brAIn) calls this; each field is optional.

name.name: Name
name.description: The name it goes by in the game, up to 16 letters.

colour.name: Colour
colour.description: The colour of its name in chat, one of Minecraft's sixteen colour names.

active.name: Active
active.description: Whether a companion is running. Switching it off takes anything it has out of the world.

model.name: Model
model.description: The model it answers with, shown on the panel.

companion_say.name: Say something as the companion
companion_say.description: A message in the game's chat under a speaker name and colour, to named players or to everyone in the game. The add-on decides nothing about who may hear what; the caller does.

to.name: To
to.description: A player's Minecraft name, a list of them, or everyone.

message.name: Message
message.description: What it says. Long messages are split over a few lines.

name.name: Speaker
name.description: The name it is said under; the companion's own name if left out.

chime.name: Chime
chime.description: Play a soft chime to each player it is said to.

companion_appear.name: Bring the companion beside a player
companion_appear.description: An invulnerable, silent allay named as the companion appears beside a player for some seconds, with a chime, sparkles and a little wave, and then goes. Logged and undoable.

ask_choice.name: Ask with choice pads
ask_choice.description: Put a two-picture question to a player. A green and a red pad go beside them with a picture above each; standing on one for two seconds is the answer, announced as the bruh_minecraft_answer event. Asked the next time they play if they are not on.

player.name: Player
player.description: The Minecraft name (Bedrock names keep their dot).

question.name: Question
question.description: The question in words, kept for the record; the player sees the pictures.

options.name: Options
options.description: Two options, each either a label, or an object with a label, a picture (a block id), a gift (an item) and a gift_count. Leave out for yes and no.

person.name: Person
person.description: What the caller calls them, for the panel.

companion_build.name: Build something small
companion_build.description: Up to 64 blocks, relative to a player's feet when a player is named. Only into empty space, on natural ground, never in a protected place or on or next to a build; logged, and undone with undo_action.

blocks.name: Blocks
blocks.description: A list of blocks, each with x, y, z and a block id, for example x 2, y 0, z 0, block oak_planks.

player.name: Beside
player.description: A Minecraft name; the coordinates are then offsets from where they stand.

dimension.name: Dimension
dimension.description: For absolute coordinates (no player); minecraft:overworld unless given.

title.name: Title
title.description: What it is, for the log ("a little bridge").

companion_edit.name: Change blocks (trusted)
companion_edit.description: Any block, anywhere — placed, replaced or removed, and boxes filled — for a person the companion's caller trusts to ask for anything. Not held to the companion's own building rules. Every block's state before is saved first, so undo_action puts it all back; a large change is backed up first.

blocks.name: Blocks
blocks.description: A list of blocks, each with x, y, z, a block state (oak_planks, red_bed[facing=east,part=head]) and an optional mode remove.

fills.name: Fills
fills.description: Boxes to fill, each with x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2 and a block (air clears it).

player.name: Beside
player.description: A Minecraft name; the coordinates are then offsets from where they stand.

dimension.name: Dimension
dimension.description: For absolute coordinates (no player); minecraft:overworld unless given.

title.name: Title
title.description: What it is, for the log ("a new bedroom").

look_blocks.name: Look at the blocks
look_blocks.description: The blocks in a box around a player or a point (at most 32 by 16 by 32), read from the saved world — every block that is not air, with its state, so a room's walls, doors and beds can be understood.

player.name: Around
player.description: A Minecraft name; the box is around where they stand.

size.name: Size
size.description: The box as three numbers, x, y and z (16, 8 and 16 unless given).

undo_action.name: Undo the companion's action
undo_action.description: Put back what one of the companion's actions changed in the world (blocks that still hold what it placed, and its entities). Leave the id out for the newest one that can still be undone.

set_zone.name: Set a place
set_zone.description: Name a place in the world (x, z, radius). Nothing is ever built inside a protected one; delete removes it. A player walking into a named place fires bruh_minecraft_place.

companion_handover.name: Hand over the old companion state
companion_handover.description: The family list, memory and settings the add-on's own companion kept in this world up to 1.17.7, for brAIn to keep once. With done, the old state is retired and not read again. Returns response data.

rename_world.name: Rename the world
rename_world.description: Rename the active world to a name as said ("Our World"). The folder takes a safe form of it (Our_World) and the server list shows the name as said. Stops the server, keeps the backups, and restarts the add-on.
